problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A={{a}_{n}\,:\,{a}_{n+2}={a}_{n+1}+2{a}_{n}\,,\,{a}_{1}=2,\,{a}_{2}=4,\,n\in N}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $A?$

examples.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements of a Set Defined Using a Recursive Sequence
examples.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A = \big \{ a_n \,:\,a_{n+1} = 2a_{n} - 1, \, a_1 = 2,\, n \in \mathbb N \big\}.
$$

Write down a set that's equivalent to $A$ using ellipsis notation.
examples.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the *recursive* sequence $a_n,$ given by

$$
a_{n+1} =2a_{n} - 1, \quad a_1 =2,\qquad n \in \mathbb N.
$$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =2 \\ {a}_{2} & =2{a}_{1}-1 \\  & =2(2)-1 \\  & =3 \\ {a}_{3} & =2{a}_{2}-1 \\  & =2(3)-1 \\  & =5 \\ {a}_{4} & =2{a}_{3}-1 \\  & =2(5)-1 \\  & =9 \\ {a}_{5} & =2{a}_{4}-1 \\  & =2(9)-1 \\  & =17 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
A = \left\{2,3,5,9,17,\ldots \right\}.
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A={{3}^{n}:n\in N}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $A?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n}={3}^{n},\,n\in N.
$$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & ={3}^{1}=3 \\ {a}_{2} & ={3}^{2}=9 \\ {a}_{3} & ={3}^{3}=27 \\ {a}_{4} & ={3}^{4}=81 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
A={3,9,27,81,…}.
$$
